name: GlobalSecureAccessSignaling
label: Enable Global Secure Access signaling for Conditional Access
helpText: Controls whether Global Secure Access signals network context to Conditional Access: source IP restoration (Conditional Access and the sign-in logs see the user's original IP instead of the service's egress IPs) and compliant network validation (sign-ins can be required to come from a verified network). Enabling it changes what existing location-based Conditional Access policies evaluate - a policy keyed on the service's egress IPs stops matching - so review those policies first. Prerequisite: the tenant must be onboarded to Global Secure Access (enable 'Onboard Global Secure Access' first); the standard reports an error naming that prerequisite until onboarding has run. Requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license.
executiveText: Makes Microsoft's cloud network security service report each user's true network location to the sign-in controls, so policies can require that sign-ins come from company devices or networks, and sign-in logs show real user IP addresses instead of a shared service address.
docsDescription: Grades signalingStatus (enabled/disabled) from the NetworkAccess cache, which is collected only for onboarded tenants. Remediation PATCHes /networkAccess/settings/conditionalAccess with the selected status. A tenant that is not onboarded is reported as an error naming the onboarding standard instead of Graph's ambiguous 403 (missing app permission or missing onboarding?).
